# Differentiate the background of the In Review header

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, all group section headers (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ▼ ──`, `── Idea (2) ──`, `── In Review (5) ──`) are rendered identically — bold, with a foreground stage colour and no background fill. The producer cannot distinguish the In Review section from other sections at a glance, which matters because In Review items are the only ones with an active producer-review obligation. Give the In Review header a grey background so the section stands out visually.

## Users

- **Herdr users (primarily the producer / session operator)** who scan the selection list for the In Review queue and need to locate that section quickly.
  - User story: "As a Herdr user reviewing the selection list, I want the In Review header to have a distinctive grey background so I can spot the review queue section immediately, even when the list is long."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour, e.g. `ANSI.bg(238)` or a nearby grey value) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other group heading rows (e.g. `Group N`, `Idea`, `Completed`, etc.) are unchanged — no background fill added.
- AC3: The selected-heading highlight still works: when the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing reverse-video selection bar (`reverseWrap`) remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, count, collapse arrow, and width-truncation behaviour are unaffected by the background change (single-row heading invariant preserved).
- AC5: Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence, and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Use existing ANSI helpers in `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.bg(code)` with a 256-colour code) — no new dependencies.
- Must not change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Implementation must be keyed off the heading's `groupLabel === 'In Review'` (the label originates in `grouping.ts`); keep the label source as the single source of truth.

## Existing state

- Group heading rows are first-class rows in the display-rows model (`DisplayHeadingRow`), interleaved by `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- The heading row is rendered in `createListRenderer` at `worklist.ts:~4482`:
  `const line = `${indent} ${ANSI.fg(stageColor(undefined))}${ANSI.bold}── ${row.groupLabel} (${row.count}) ${arrow} ──${ANSI.reset}``
- `ANSI.bg(code)` exists at `worklist.ts:~345` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`) and is already used for banner fills (e.g. `ANSI.bg(196)`, `ANSI.bg(220)`, `ANSI.bg(40)`).
- The `In Review` group label is assigned in `grouping.ts:~309` (`groupLabel: 'In Review'` for `stage === 'in_review'`).
- Selected rows are wrapped with `reverseWrap` (re-asserts `\x1b[0m` resets to keep the whole selected row highlighted); heading rows have no interior resets so they are handled fine.

## Desired change

- In the heading-row render branch of `createListRenderer`, when `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, wrap the line's base style with a grey background (`${ANSI.bg(238)}` or similar), keeping the existing foreground/bold styling and the existing `reverseWrap` interaction on selection. Other headings render as today.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch (`createListRenderer`, ~line 4482); add conditional grey background for `groupLabel === 'In Review'`; `ANSI.bg` helper at ~line 345.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — extend with tests asserting the background escape sequence on `In Review` headings and its absence on others.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageColor`/ANSI conventions (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- Grey background may reduce contrast against the 220 (yellow-ish) foreground `stageColor` for in-review headings; mitigate by choosing a dark grey (238) and verifying readability. If contrast is insufficient, the foreground can be switched to white (231) for this heading only — record the choice in the implementation.
- Selection visibility: reverse-wrap must stay visible over the background — covered by AC3; verify selection rendering in a terminal, not just by string matching.
- Scope creep: do NOT extend the background to other headings unless separately requested — that is a separate work item (recorded here to avoid accidental bundling).
- Test brittleness: assert on the presence of the `\x1b[48;5;...m` background sequence for the In Review heading rather than on exact full-row strings, to avoid coupling to foreground/bold detail changes.

## Related work

- **Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping completed item found. Related completed items (none duplicates): WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9 (total actionable count in Herdr header), WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB (in_progress/in_review in mandatory In Review set), WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ (selection-list refresh on tab focus), WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 (heading rows as first-class display rows — this feature builds on that model).
- `docs/icons-design.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed description ("make the In Review header background gray (or similar) to differentiate that section from other sections") was specific enough to draft the brief directly. Assumption recorded: "gray (or similar)" means a grey ANSI 256 background (default candidate: 238, same value already used elsewhere in `worklist.ts`), applied only to the In Review heading; other section headers remain unchanged. Rationale: description explicitly scopes differentiation to "that section".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKW1GUSC1DSWYGS** – OpenCode (completed)
- **WL-0ML1LBF6H0NE40RX** – Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes (completed)
- **WL-0ML4DOK1U19NN8LG** – Add wl list --parent <id> for child-only listing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection, similar
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
data.title: Differentiate the background of the In Review header

# Grey background on In Review heading

## Summary

In `createListRenderer`'s heading-row branch, give the heading whose `groupLabel === 'In Review'` a grey ANSI 256 background fill while leaving every other heading unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour via the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper, default `ANSI.bg(238)`) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other heading rows (`Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `Completed`, etc.) render exactly as before — no background escape added.
- AC3: When the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing `reverseWrap(line)` selection bar remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, item count, collapse arrow (`▼`/`▶`), depth indentation, and width truncation are unchanged; the single-row heading invariant and line-count accounting are preserved.
- AC5: The grey choice keeps the heading legible; if contrast against the existing foreground is insufficient, switch this heading's foreground to white (`ANSI.fg(231)`) and record the choice in a code comment.
- AC6: The full project test suite passes with the change (run via the project test skill).
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (on the heading-render branch) and the relevant section of `packages/herdr/README.md` (and any relevant wiki or docs site entries).

## Constraints

- Use the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper in `worklist.ts` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`, ~line 357) — no new dependencies.
- Do NOT change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Key the condition off `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, keeping the label source (`grouping.ts` ~line 309) as the single source of truth.
- Do NOT extend the background to other headings — that is out of scope.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch in `createListRenderer` (~line 4482) and the `ANSI.bg` helper (~line 357).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions to update for AC7.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `const bg = row.groupLabel === 'In Review' ? ANSI.bg(238) : '';` in the heading branch and prepend it to the line's base style (keep foreground + bold + trailing `ANSI.reset`).

## Deliverables

- Updated `worklist.ts` heading render branch implementing AC1–AC5; doc/comment updates (AC7); suite green (AC6). Resolution of the grey/contrast choice recorded in a code comment (AC5).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Test: In Review heading background rendering` (test-first ordering, parent AC5); dependency edge wired.

# Tests: Pi extension X-Priority header injection

Test-first unit tests for the Worklog pi extension module that turns the pane-launch environment variable into the `X-Priority` provider request header (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC4).

## Goal
Executable specs in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts` covering valid, invalid and unset `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` values and the `before_provider_headers` hook registration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Valid values:** `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` of `low`, `medium` or `high` causes the hook to set `X-Priority` to that exact value on the outgoing header map.
- [ ] **Unset value:** with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` absent or empty, the header map is returned untouched (no `X-Priority` added; the proxy applies its own `medium` default).
- [ ] **Invalid value:** any other value (`fast`, `HIGH`, `critical`, whitespace, etc.) leaves the header map untouched.
- [ ] **Hook registration:** the extension module registers a `before_provider_headers` hook when loaded, and the hook is side-effect free when the env var is unset.
- [ ] Tests are colocated at `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts` and are initially red.

## Key Files
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts`

## Notes
- Fail-open is mandatory: a missing/invalid value must never inject an assumed `high`.
- Source of truth for the env contract is the parent description (`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, values `low|medium|high`).

# Tests: downtime priority & retired-settings backward compatibility

Test-first unit tests for the downtime dispatch priority environment and for backward-compatible loading of retired `modeSwitch*` settings keys (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC3/AC5).

## Goal
Executable specs in the downtime-worker and settings test modules proving the downtime priority table, the fixed serial Phase-2 parallelism, and that retired settings keys are ignored rather than rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Downtime env mapping:** tests prove `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (or its successor) sets `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` from the selected `DowntimeCandidate.priority`: `low`→`low`, `medium`→`medium`, `high`→`high`, `critical`→`high`, unknown/absent→`medium`.
- [ ] **Serial Phase 2:** tests prove `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is always `'1'`, whatever config/priority/free-slot inputs are supplied, and that the env-building function no longer accepts mode/slot-budget plumbing.
- [ ] **Retired settings load:** a settings file containing `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` and `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` still loads successfully, those keys are absent from the parsed settings object, and no defaults are emitted for them.
- [ ] Tests are colocated with `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` and are initially red.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (priority + parallelism)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` (backward compatibility)

- AC5 fixes parallelism at `1` by producer decision; do not parameterise it.

# Implement: Remove mode-switch machinery, serial Phase 2

Remove the client half of the retired fast/cheap operating mode and fix audit Phase-2 parallelism to serial (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC1/AC5).

## Goal
Herdr no longer contains or configures a mode-switch worker, sends no `/admin/set-mode` calls, exposes no `modeSwitch*` settings, and always runs audit Phase 2 serially; the plugin starts and dispatches normally.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`, `mode-switch-worker.test.ts`, `mode-switch-integration.test.ts` and `drain-regression-guard.test.ts` are deleted.
- [ ] The `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` and `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` settings (types, defaults, parsing, clamping, validation) are removed from `settings.ts`; existing settings files containing those keys still load (keys ignored, no migration).
- [ ] The `mode-switch` scheduler task and its worker/poll-interval options/imports are removed from `worklist.ts`.
- [ ] `index.ts` no longer constructs or holds the worker, wires `onProxyIdle`/`onOperatorCommand`, or passes an observed `mode` to the downtime dispatcher; every `/admin/set-mode` call is gone.
- [ ] `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is always `'1'`; `DowntimeSpawnConfig` and its `mode`/`slotBudget`/`freeSlots`/`concurrentDispatchCap` plumbing are deleted while the existing free-slot dispatch gating is unchanged.
- [ ] The package builds, the changed-scope tests (including the F3 backward-compatibility specs) pass, and the plugin starts and dispatches in an existing dispatch test.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Delete the four worker/test files.
2. Strip `modeSwitch*` from `settings.ts` defaults/parse/validation; keep permissive loading of unknown keys.
3. Remove the `mode-switch` scheduler task and options from `worklist.ts`.
4. Remove worker construction, holder, callbacks and mode passing from `index.ts`.
5. Collapse `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` to a constant `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '1'` and delete `DowntimeSpawnConfig` and its call-site plumbing in `downtime-worker.ts`.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` (delete)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`, `mode-switch-integration.test.ts`, `drain-regression-guard.test.ts` (delete)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`, `settings.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`

# Audit-batch dispatch — test specs (test-first)

Test-first companion to WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Write the FAILING test specs for depth-aware audit batching BEFORE any implementation. The specs pin the behaviours in parent AC1–AC5 so the implementation items (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS children C3–C5) verify against them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`: `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` clamps to [1, 5], non-finite falls back to the default (2), `1` = legacy/off; `loadSettings` parses `downtimeAuditBatchMax` from a fixture config (valid, invalid, missing).
2. `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` (parent AC6a): shallow depth (< `browseItemCount`) keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour — exactly one dispatch and a full idle-tracker reset (`tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`) after it, and no `audit-batch-continue` token.
3. `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6b): depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces exactly N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window, each continuation gated by a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check.
4. `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6c): an unsatisfied idle-duration gate and sub-2 free slots block ALL dispatch including continuations; `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` is never relaxed.
5. `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6d): a non-stale host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation; the continuation proceeds only after the marker is released.
6. `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (AC6e, AC6f, AC4): the cap and the depth-drop end the batch and restore single-dispatch behaviour; dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice; a failed CAS claim / spawn failure / any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch; in coordination mode the leader defers the own-backlog leadership hand-off until batch end.
7. Every spec is runnable against the current tree (red) — each uses only the current public API (dispatch functions, worker object, settings loaders) and existing fixture/stub patterns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `describe`/`it` blocks to the five test files in the parent's Key Files using the existing mock-deps / `createDowntimeWorker` / `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchFromCoordination` patterns.
- Assert on dispatch outcome (`dispatched`, `kind`, `reason`), the idle tracker state, the decision-log entries (tokens + metadata), and leadership state (`isLeader`) — never on wall-clock timing.
- Run the herdr package suite via the test skill to confirm the new specs fail as expected against the current tree.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts

## Dependencies

- None (test-first — the implementation items depend on this spec).

## Deliverables

- Red (failing) spec blocks covering parent AC6(a)–(f) and AC5 tokens, committed to dev before any implementation.

# Settings: `downtimeAuditBatchMax` (DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX)

Add the bounded audit-batch cap setting that opts into depth-aware audit batching (parent AC1). `1` = legacy/off (current behaviour); default `2`; clamped to a safe range. Same plumbing pattern as `downtimeMaxAttempts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = 2`; `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` clamps to [1, 5]; non-finite/NaN input falls back to the default (2); `1` is accepted and means batching off.
2. `PluginSettings` gains `downtimeAuditBatchMax`, present in `defaultSettings`, parsed in `loadSettings` (valid numbers pass through clamped; missing/invalid fall back to the default) and saved by `saveSettings`.
3. `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()` exposes `auditBatchMax?: number` (optional, backward-compatible) and it is threaded through `createDowntimeWorker`'s dispatch options to both `dispatchDowntimeWork` and `dispatchFromCoordination`.
4. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` wires the live setting (re-read each tick, like `browseItemCount`/`maxAttempts`) into the worker config.
5. Settings tests in the test-first spec item (C1) pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = 2`, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MIN = 1`, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = 5` and `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` in `downtime-worker.ts` (mirroring `clampDowntimeMaxAttempts`).
- Extend `PluginSettings` / `defaultSettings` / `loadSettings` in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.
- Add `auditBatchMax?: number` to `DowntimeWorkerConfig.config()` and forward `cfg.auditBatchMax` into the dispatch options in `tick()`; wire the setting in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Update file-header/key-file comments that enumerate downtime settings.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/settings.ts

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts

## Dependencies

## Deliverables

# Depth-derived batch activation + conditional idle reset in `tick()`

Core of parent AC1/AC2/AC3: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head, activate a bounded batch budget only when the queue is deep, and replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one scoped strictly to an audit-batch continuation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Depth computation (AC1).** A helper derives the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head: count items where `classifyItemForDispatch(item, now) === 'audit'` (root `completed`/`in_review`, excluding fresh-audited, producer-review, assignee-held and soft-deleted items). No new `wl` subprocess is added to the common dispatch path.
2. **Activation rule (AC1).** Batch mode is active only when `depth >= browseItemCount` AND `auditBatchMax > 1`; otherwise behaviour is byte-for-byte today's: one dispatch per idle window followed by a full idle-tracker reset.
3. **Batch budget state (AC1/AC3).** An in-memory per-worker budget (like `lastDispatchAt`/`cooldownUntil`) counts audit dispatches in the current batch, is initialised to `auditBatchMax` when a batch activates, and is cleared when: the cap is reached, the depth drops below the threshold, a non-audit dispatch occurs, an audit dispatch ends in any non-`dispatched` outcome (including `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back`, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`, `anchor-unavailable`), the worker pauses/cooldowns, or leadership is lost.
4. **Conditional idle reset (AC2).** On a successful **audit** dispatch while a batch is active with budget remaining, `tick()` does NOT call `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`; for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, today's reset is preserved exactly. Every gate (idle-duration threshold, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, `slotOwned`, `contention_queue_depth == 0`, code-freeze, host-wide/per-worklog audit markers, single-flight) is still re-checked on every tick, including continuations — no gate is relaxed or bypassed.
5. **No duplicate / no target skipping (AC3).** Continuations flow through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A continuation never skips to a different target after a failed outcome — the batch simply ends.
6. **Regression safety.** Non-audit dispatch (critical/implement/plan/intake/risk-effort) still resets the tracker and never arms a batch even when the queue is deep; legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`) keeps its existing tier-chain semantics.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `computeAuditEligibleDepth(items, now)` (or equivalent) beside `readReviewQueueGate` in `downtime-worker.ts`; reuse `classifyItemForDispatch` — no second eligibility definition.
- Add `auditBatch` worker-scope state (cap, remaining, active flag) and a `shouldDeferIdleReset(outcome, depth, cap)` decision helper (pure, exported for tests).
- In `tick()`: after a successful dispatch, look at `outcome.kind === 'audit'`, the current depth and the remaining budget, then conditionally skip the reset; clear the budget on every batch-ending condition listed in AC3.
- Extend `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` with the minimal machine-readable surface the worker needs (e.g. `auditBatchEligible?: boolean`), documented in the interface comment.
- Cover with the specs from C1 plus any new unit tests for the pure helpers.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the settings/plumbing item (C2) for `auditBatchMax`.

## Deliverables

- Depth helper + batch budget + conditional reset, with green audit-tier/dispatch/orchestrator tests.
data.title: Depth-derived batch activation + conditional idle reset

# Coordination-mode batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

Parent AC4: on the production coordination path the leader must source continuation audit targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking) without releasing leadership mid-batch, and defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Continuation source (AC4).** After a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, `dispatchFromCoordination` may dispatch the next audit target from the leader's own head extension (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `includeNonCritical` filter as today) instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion — still exactly one dispatch per invocation, never two.
2. **Same filters (AC3/AC4).** Every own-head continuation passes the identical sequential filters as the existing own-backlog fallback: `classifyItemForDispatch`, dispatched-marker exclusion (id-guard + staleness), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, audit slot minimum (≥2), in-flight critical guard, review-queue hold for implements. The continuation selects only `audit`-kind items.
3. **No duplicate target (AC3).** The item just dispatched, and any item already dispatched in this batch, is never re-selected in the same batch — enforced by the existing marker exclusion plus an explicit batch-local exclusion set, covered by a test.
4. **Leadership timing (AC4).** An own-backlog (`ownBacklogDispatch === true`) audit dispatch during an active batch with budget remaining does NOT trigger `releaseLeadership()` in that tick; the step-down happens exactly once at batch end (cap reached, depth dropped, failed continuation, or the next tick when the batch is no longer active). A normal in-view dispatch is unchanged.
5. **No regression.** Non-batch coordination dispatch, leader election/lease TTL, coordination check-ins, pruning and the offer path are unchanged; `dispatchFromCoordination` direct-API callers without `freeSlots`/`auditBatchMax` keep today's behaviour (fail-open).

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread `auditBatchMax` and the batch-continuation intent through `dispatchFromCoordination`'s options (a boolean/marker set by `tick()` when the batch is active, plus the dispatched-target set for the current batch).
- Factor the existing own-backlog candidate loop into a reusable helper so the continuation path applies the exact same filters (no duplicated filter chain).
- Add `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` (and any needed batch metadata) to `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, documented, so `tick()` can decide the leadership step-down and the idle-reset deferral without re-deriving state.
- In `tick()`, gate the existing `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true` step-down on batch-inactive (deferring it to batch end).
- Cover with the coordination-dispatch and orchestrator specs from C1.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and outcome surface.
- Depends on the observability item (C5) for the continuation token contract.

## Deliverables

- Leader own-head continuation with unchanged filter semantics and deferred step-down, with green coordination-dispatch/orchestrator tests.

# Observability: audit-batch decision tokens and metadata

Parent AC5: every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log at the existing rate limit. Existing reason tokens are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Continuation token (AC5).** An accepted audit-batch continuation records a distinct token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`) in the existing decision log with metadata: `depth`, `cap`, `remaining`, plus today's standard fields (`freeSlots`, `totalSlots`, `ownerPresent`, `runningPanes`, `contentionDepth`).
2. **Blocked continuation tokens (AC5).** Held/blocked continuations reuse the existing tokens unchanged — `audit-in-flight` (per-worklog single-flight) and `audit-host-saturated` (host-wide marker) for marker blocks, `slot-owned`, `proxy-contention`, `code-freeze`, `review-queue-hold`, `no-candidate` — with the batch metadata (depth/cap/remaining) attached when a batch was active.
3. **Batch end observability.** Batch deactivation transitions that would otherwise be silent surface in the decision log where a distinct signal adds value (e.g. cap reached / depth dropped) without spamming the log — still rate-limited by `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`.
4. **Rate limiting + header unchanged.** The header blocking token updates on every refusal exactly as today; `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` behaviour is preserved for refusals; no existing reason-token test regresses.
5. **Doc alignment.** The new/attached tokens match the token list committed in the docs item (C6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the decision-log entry shape (`CoordinationLogEntry` kind `decision`) with optional `batch?: { depth: number; cap: number; remaining: number }` + the `audit-batch-continue`/`audit-batch-held`(if distinct signal) reasons routed through the worker's `recordDecision`.
- Emit the continuation token from `tick()` after a batch-armed continuation attempt (accepted or held) with the live depth/cap/remaining; re-compute depth from the head the same way as C3.
- Update the reason-token comment blocks in `downtime-worker.ts` and the dispatcher doc token list (§~60/108).
- Cover with the decision-log specs from C1 (`downtime-log.test.ts`).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md (token list)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and depth computation.

## Deliverables

- Observable batch decisions (token + depth/cap/remaining metadata) with green token/metadata specs.

# Documentation: batch setting, activation rule, sequential-safety invariants and decision tokens

Parent AC7: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, its activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation (incl. code comments) is updated and consistent with shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher doc.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents:
   - the setting (`downtimeAuditBatchMax`, default 2, clamped 1–5, `1` = legacy/off) — in the settings table (~§1638) and the configuration prose;
   - the activation rule (audit-eligible depth ≥ `browseItemCount` from the Herdr head + `auditBatchMax > 1`);
   - the sequential single-audit safety invariants (AC2 gate list — nothing relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset deferred);
   - the new decision tokens (`audit-batch-continue` and held/blocked variants) in the reason-token lists (~§60/108) and observations section;
   - the deferred own-backlog leadership hand-off (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 interplay).
2. **README.** `packages/herdr/README.md` adds an operator-facing bullet for `downtimeAuditBatchMax` in the settings list (~§521) and notes the batching behaviour (sequentially within one idle window, at most one active audit) in the audit-dispatch section.
3. **Code comments.** Comments in `downtime-worker.ts` / `settings.ts` / `index.ts` describing the batch mode, its lifecycle and trade-offs (incl. the proxy-busy caveat: the audit pane's own occupancy still resets the tracker; the deferred reset is only the dispatcher's own post-dispatch reset) match the shipped behaviour in C3–C5.
4. **Consistency.** Every documented token, setting name and activation rule matches the implementation; a doc-consistency scan (C7) finds no stale single-dispatch-only claims.
